basis: Neurodevelopmental disorder; strabismus and congenital muscular torticollis each affect 1/3, supporting ocular dysfunction and structural muscle involvement; sampling is limited.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus represents impaired ocular alignment, reported in 1/3 patients; the frequency meets the threshold, although the sample is small.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: congenital muscular torticollis is structural muscle dysfunction, reported in 1/3 patients; neurologic hypotonia alone would not qualify.

basis: Choanal obstruction, thyroid abnormalities and hearing loss define the syndrome. Lacrimal anomalies lack established functional impairment; amblyopia and microphthalmia each occur in 1/9.

decisions.ocular: none: unspecified lacrimal duct anomalies do not establish impaired drainage; damaging ocular findings, amblyopia and microphthalmia, each occur in only 1/9.

basis: Inherited generalized proximal tubular failure is defined by renal solute wasting, including phosphate, electrolyte and bicarbonate losses with metabolic disturbances.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: electrolyte wasting and acid-base disturbances are defining components of generalized Fanconi syndrome, rather than occasional extra-renal complications.

basis: Complex congenital cardiac malformations predominate. Asplenia occurs in 4/14 (~29%), below the frequency threshold; abnormal visceral position alone does not establish damage.

decisions.haematologic: none: asplenia occurs in 4/14 (~29%), below the qualifying frequency and not a required diagnostic feature; this is a borderline exclusion.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment, growth hormone deficiency and hearing loss/aural atresia are common defining features. Hypothyroidism alone is occasional (5-29%).

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the definition explicitly identifies growth hormone deficiency among common defining features; occasional hypothyroidism does not negate this endocrine involvement.
decisions.otologic: primary: hearing loss and aural atresia are explicitly common features in the syndrome's own definition.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment and epilepsy define the disorder. Joint hypermobility occurs in 80-99%, but accompanying joint injury or functional loss is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint hypermobility (80-99%) alone does not establish damaging joint disease; generalized hypotonia can reflect the primary neurologic disorder.

basis: An inborn coenzyme A metabolic defect causes neurodegeneration; retinal dystrophy and optic pallor occur in 30-79%. Stiffness and dysphagia reflect neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: PKAN is an established inborn disorder of coenzyme A metabolism, supporting the metabolic mechanism axis alongside neurologic disease.

basis: C1q-associated autoimmune lupus causes cutaneous disease in ~90% and nephritis in ~30-40%; arthritis is reported in roughly 20-25%, below threshold.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: arthritis in C1q-associated lupus is approximately 20-25%; the higher joint involvement of ordinary SLE should not be transferred to this subtype.

basis: Skeletal deformities and mitral regurgitation occur in 1/1 annotated patient, supporting structural skeletal and cardiac dysfunction; generalizability from one patient is uncertain.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: mitral regurgitation represents cardiac valve dysfunction and occurs in 1/1 annotated patient; the single-patient evidence limits confidence.

basis: Metabolic deficiency with defining neurologic and hepatic presentations; developmental delay 80-99%, hepatic encephalopathy 30-79%. Cardiomyopathy occurs in only 5-29%.

decisions.hepatic: primary: liver disease is explicitly a defining presentation, supported by hepatomegaly and hepatic encephalopathy at 30-79%; it is not merely a later risk.
decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment and later-onset neurologic dysfunction explicitly define presentations; neurodevelopmental delay occurs in 80-99%.
